title: Waking
hook: many Christians make their first thought a prayer, before the phone
tomorrow: can you give away a day before you've seen it?

segments.voice: Yesterday the saints' long stretch closed with a book on a table, and the line keep reading them. Now a new stretch, living it, and it starts at the very first minute.

The alarm goes off, and the phone is right there, and so is everything in it: the news, the group chat, the inbox. Here's an odd detail in Mark's Gospel. The night before, the whole town of Capernaum crowded at the door where Jesus was staying. He was the one everybody wanted. And in the morning, “rising up a great while before day,” he slips out to a solitary place to pray. When Simon tracks him down, he says, “All men seek for thee.” So why leave the people who were looking for him?
screen: `THE PHONE IS RIGHT THERE.` → `THE WHOLE TOWN AT THE DOOR.` → `SO WHY SLIP OUT BEFORE DAWN?`

segments.voice: Read one more line and the puzzle solves itself. Jesus answers Simon: “Let us go into the next towns, that I may preach there also.” He doesn't go back to the crowd at the door. Something in that early hour set the direction of the day before anyone else's wants could. The first voice he listened to wasn't the town's. The Psalms had already put the morning first. Psalm five: “My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.” Direct, like aiming. Look up, like waiting for an answer. Psalm one hundred thirty-nine gives the gentlest version: “when I awake, I am still with thee.” Not I'd better start talking to God now, but God was already there while I slept. Christians have built small habits on lines like these. Some say a verse before standing up. Some make the sign of the cross. Some just say thank you. The words matter less than the order. The first thought goes to God; the phone, the news and the worry still come, they just don't get to speak first. One to tell a friend tonight: in Mark, the dawn prayer is what sends Jesus somewhere new, not back to where he was wanted.
screen: `LET US GO INTO THE NEXT TOWNS.` · `MY VOICE SHALT THOU HEAR IN THE MORNING.` · `WHEN I AWAKE, I AM STILL WITH THEE.` · `GOD FIRST, THE PHONE SECOND.` · then, large: `FIRST THOUGHT, GOD.`

segments.voice: Sit the way you do when you've just woken, with your phone face down and out of reach. Let your hands rest open, and choose the first words you'll give tomorrow morning before the screen: perhaps when I awake, I am still with thee, or a plain thank you.
Waking. The first minute of the day, given to God before the phone, the news or the worry.
Pocket this one: first thought, God, and everything else gets the second. See you in the morning.

chat.meaning: The habit is the order, not the hour: the first thought goes to God, and the phone and the worry come second.

Simon.meaning: Simon Peter, one of Jesus' first followers

Mark.meaning: the Gospel of Mark, one of the four Gospels

sign of the cross.meaning: tracing a cross over the body as a gesture of prayer
